explanation_en: A strong, emphatic way of denying or disagreeing with a statement. It is much more forceful than a simple 'no' and is suitable for both formal debates and casual conversations.

examples.en_text: By no means am I going to accept that contract without reading it first.
examples.target_text: De ninguna manera voy a aceptar ese contrato sin leerlo antes.

examples.en_text: By no means do I want you to think it was your fault.
examples.target_text: De ninguna manera quiero que pienses que fue culpa tuya.

examples.en_text: There is no way you are going out in this storm.
examples.target_text: De ninguna manera vas a salir a la calle con esta tormenta.

examples.en_text: We cannot allow this mistake to happen under any circumstances.
examples.target_text: No podemos permitir que este error ocurra de ninguna manera.

examples.en_text: By no means am I going to miss the opportunity to travel this year.
examples.target_text: De ninguna manera voy a perder la oportunidad de viajar este año.

examples.en_text: Do you want to cancel the project? Absolutely not! We have worked hard on it.
examples.target_text: ¿Quieres cancelar el proyecto? ¡De ninguna manera! Hemos trabajado mucho en él.

explanation_en: Indicates doing something according to one's unique style, method, or standard, often implying a non-traditional or unexpected approach.

examples.en_text: She paints in her own way, without following the traditional rules of the school.
examples.target_text: Ella pinta a su manera, sin seguir las reglas tradicionales de la escuela.

examples.en_text: Each of my children solves problems in their own way.
examples.target_text: Cada uno de mis hijos resuelve los problemas a su manera.

examples.en_text: He is a bit cold, but he loves you in his own way.
examples.target_text: Él es un poco frío, pero te quiere a su manera.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, she will organize the office in her own way and it will turn out very well.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes, ella organizará la oficina a su manera y quedará muy bien.

examples.en_text: This city is chaotic, but it has charm in its own way.
examples.target_text: Esta ciudad es caótica, pero tiene encanto a su manera.

examples.en_text: The musicians decided to play the song in their own way, giving it a jazz style.
examples.target_text: Los músicos decidieron tocar la canción a su manera, dándole un estilo de jazz.

explanation_en: Used when summarizing or paraphrasing the core message of what someone said or implied. It helps shift the focus from literal words to the underlying meaning.

examples.en_text: The boss's email basically says that we have to work faster.
examples.target_text: El correo del jefe viene a decir que tenemos que trabajar más rápido.

examples.en_text: These articles basically say that the economy is going to improve soon.
examples.target_text: Estos artículos vienen a decir que la economía va a mejorar pronto.

examples.en_text: What he was basically saying is that he doesn't agree with the plan.
examples.target_text: Lo que él venía a decir es que no está de acuerdo con el plan.

examples.en_text: The new law basically says that smoking is no longer allowed on terraces.
examples.target_text: La nueva ley viene a decir que ya no se puede fumar en las terrazas.

examples.en_text: With that look, you're basically telling me that you don't feel like going out today.
examples.target_text: Con esa mirada, me vienes a decir que no tienes ganas de salir hoy.

examples.en_text: The last chapter of the book basically says that happiness depends on us.
examples.target_text: El último capítulo del libro viene a decir que la felicidad depende de nosotros.

explanation_en: Means to exceed a limit, standard, or expectation, or to delve deeper into an issue. It is a very common B2/C1 transition phrase in argumentative speech.

examples.en_text: The new phones don't just have a better camera, but they go a step further with artificial intelligence.
examples.target_text: Los nuevos teléfonos no solo tienen mejor cámara, sino que van un poco más allá con la inteligencia artificial.

examples.en_text: In this meeting, we don't just want to look at the problems; we are going a step further to find solutions.
examples.target_text: En esta reunión no queremos solo ver los problemas, sino que vamos un poco más allá para buscar soluciones.

examples.en_text: This movie isn't a simple comedy; it goes a step further and makes us reflect on life.
examples.target_text: Esta película no es una simple comedia; va un poco más allá y nos hace reflexionar sobre la vida.

examples.en_text: If you want to stand out at work, I suggest you go a step further than what they ask of you.
examples.target_text: Si quieres destacar en el trabajo, te sugiero que vayas un poco más allá de lo que te piden.

examples.en_text: The scientists didn't just stick to the basic theory; they went a step further and proved it with experiments.
examples.target_text: Los científicos no se quedaron con la teoría básica, sino que fueron un poco más allá y la demostraron con experimentos.

examples.en_text: To improve the recipe, I would go a step further and add a touch of lemon.
examples.target_text: Para mejorar la receta, yo iría un poco más allá y le añadiría un toque de limón.

explanation_en: A formal prepositional phrase used to attribute an action, attitude, or responsibility to a specific group or individual. It is a staple of journalistic and academic Spanish.

examples.en_text: I received a lot of support from my family during the exam.
examples.target_text: Recibí mucho apoyo por parte de mi familia durante el examen.

examples.en_text: There was a lack of communication on the part of the company.
examples.target_text: Hubo una falta de comunicación por parte de la empresa.

examples.en_text: We need more effort on the part of the students.
examples.target_text: Necesitamos más esfuerzo por parte de los estudiantes.

examples.en_text: There was no response on the part of the government.
examples.target_text: No hubo ninguna respuesta por parte del gobierno.

examples.en_text: The customer appreciated the good service from the staff.
examples.target_text: El cliente agradeció la buena atención por parte del personal.

examples.en_text: It was a great game on the part of both teams.
examples.target_text: Fue un gran partido por parte de ambos equipos.

explanation_en: A very common, slightly formal synonym for 'hacer' or 'realizar'. It is used to describe executing a plan, task, project, or duty.

examples.en_text: The scientists are carrying out a study on climate change.
examples.target_text: Los científicos llevan a cabo un estudio sobre el cambio climático.

examples.en_text: The students carry out their research projects in the library.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes llevan a cabo sus proyectos de investigación en la biblioteca.

examples.en_text: Local authorities are carrying out reforms to improve public transportation.
examples.target_text: Las autoridades locales llevan a cabo reformas para mejorar el transporte público.

examples.en_text: The doctors are performing a very complex operation today.
examples.target_text: Los médicos llevan a cabo una operación muy compleja hoy.

examples.en_text: The detectives are carrying out a detailed investigation into the case.
examples.target_text: Los detectives llevan a cabo una investigación detallada sobre el caso.

examples.en_text: The neighbors are carrying out activities to clean up the neighborhood park.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos llevan a cabo actividades para limpiar el parque del barrio.

explanation_en: This expression means to carry on with daily life, socialize, or go out and be active in the community. It is often used when recovering from a disruption, like a pandemic or a personal crisis, to emphasize returning to normal social routines. It is very common in everyday spoken Spanish.

examples.en_text: After the surgery, the doctor told me I could already go back to my normal life.
examples.target_text: Después de la operación, el médico me dijo que ya podía hacer vida normal.

examples.en_text: They decided to move in together to start sharing their lives.
examples.target_text: Decidieron mudarse juntos para empezar a hacer vida en común.

examples.en_text: Since she works from home, she finds it harder to have a social life.
examples.target_text: Desde que trabaja desde casa, le cuesta más hacer vida social.

examples.en_text: In this town, the neighbors prefer to spend their time out in the main square.
examples.target_text: En este pueblo, los vecinos prefieren hacer vida en la plaza.

examples.en_text: We reserve weekends to stay home and spend time as a family.
examples.target_text: Los fines de semana los reservamos para estar en casa y hacer vida familiar.

examples.en_text: Despite his age, my grandfather still lives like a young man.
examples.target_text: A pesar de su edad, mi abuelo sigue haciendo vida de joven.

explanation_en: While literally 'to know nothing,' in this context it means 'to have heard nothing from' or 'to have no news about' someone. It is a very common idiomatic way to express a lack of contact or updates about a person. It is used in everyday speech as well as in journalism.

examples.en_text: The doctors still don't know anything about the test results.
examples.target_text: Los médicos todavía no saben nada sobre los resultados de los análisis.

examples.en_text: Since he went to live abroad, we haven't heard anything from him.
examples.target_text: Desde que se fue a vivir al extranjero, no sabemos nada de él.

examples.en_text: I don't know anything about the new project; the boss hasn't said anything yet.
examples.target_text: No sé nada del nuevo proyecto; el jefe no ha dicho nada todavía.

examples.en_text: Don't tell María anything, she still doesn't know anything about the surprise party.
examples.target_text: No le digas nada a María, ella todavía no sabe nada de la fiesta sorpresa.

examples.en_text: The police are investigating the robbery, but for now they know nothing.
examples.target_text: La policía está investigando el robo, pero por ahora no saben nada.

examples.en_text: Her parents are very worried because they haven't heard anything from her since yesterday.
examples.target_text: Sus padres están muy preocupados porque no saben nada de ella desde ayer.

explanation_en: This extremely common adverbial locution means gradually or step by step. It is preferred over 'gradualmente' in almost all spoken contexts due to its natural, rhythmic flow. It can modify verbs to show progressive action over time.

examples.en_text: Little by little, I'm starting to understand native Spanish speakers.
examples.target_text: Poco a poco, estoy empezando a entender a los hablantes nativos de español.

examples.en_text: After the surgery, my grandfather recovered his mobility little by little.
examples.target_text: Después de la operación, mi abuelo recuperó la movilidad poco a poco.

examples.en_text: If you work hard, gradually you will achieve all your professional goals.
examples.target_text: Si trabajas duro, poco a poco conseguirás todas tus metas profesionales.

examples.en_text: We met at university and, gradually, we became best friends.
examples.target_text: Nos conocimos en la universidad y, poco a poco, nos convertimos en mejores amigos.

examples.en_text: At first it was hard to live in London, but little by little I got used to the weather.
examples.target_text: Al principio fue difícil vivir en Londres, pero poco a poco me acostumbré al clima.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about the mess; we are going to clean the house little by little this weekend.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes por el desorden; vamos a limpiar la casa poco a poco este fin de semana.

explanation_en: This idiom literally means 'to take the leap' or 'to jump.' In the context of migration, it specifically refers to attempting to cross a border fence. In broader contexts, it is used metaphorically to mean taking a big risk or making a major life transition (e.g., starting a new business).

examples.en_text: After working ten years in the office, he decided to take the leap and start his own company.
examples.target_text: Después de trabajar diez años en la oficina, decidió dar el salto y crear su propia empresa.

examples.en_text: I have always wanted to live abroad, but I'm a bit afraid to make the jump.
examples.target_text: Siempre he querido vivir en el extranjero, pero me da un poco de miedo dar el salto.

examples.en_text: Many traditional companies have not yet made the leap to the digital world.
examples.target_text: Muchas empresas tradicionales todavía no han dado el salto al mundo digital.

examples.en_text: If you want to improve your professional future, you have to take the leap and learn English.
examples.target_text: Si quieres mejorar tu futuro profesional, tienes que dar el salto y aprender inglés.

examples.en_text: They have been dating for five years and are finally going to take the leap of moving in together.
examples.target_text: Llevan cinco años de novios y por fin van a dar el salto de irse a vivir juntos.

examples.en_text: She always wrote in secret, but this year she took the leap and published her first novel.
examples.target_text: Ella siempre escribía en secreto, pero este año dio el salto y publicó su primera novela.

explanation_en: This figurative expression means to introduce a topic, issue, or proposal for discussion or consideration. It is widely used in political, journalistic, and business contexts. It is the direct equivalent of the English 'to put on the table' or 'to bring to the table.'

examples.en_text: In the meeting, the boss put the issue of salaries on the table.
examples.target_text: En la reunión, el jefe puso sobre la mesa el tema de los salarios.

examples.en_text: We have to put our differences on the table to solve this problem.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que poner sobre la mesa nuestras diferencias para resolver este problema.

examples.en_text: The marketing team has put several interesting proposals on the table.
examples.target_text: El equipo de marketing ha puesto sobre la mesa varias propuestas interesantes.

examples.en_text: If you don't put a better offer on the table, we won't sign the contract.
examples.target_text: Si no pones una oferta mejor sobre la mesa, no firmaremos el contrato.

examples.en_text: The new law puts the debate about climate change back on the table.
examples.target_text: La nueva ley vuelve a poner sobre la mesa el debate sobre el cambio climático.

examples.en_text: I want to put all the options on the table before we make a decision.
examples.target_text: Quiero poner todas las opciones sobre la mesa antes de que tomemos una decisión.

explanation_en: This expression means 'to take a turn' or 'to take a twist,' indicating a change in direction, development, or tone of a situation. It is commonly followed by adjectives like 'inesperado' (unexpected), 'radical' (radical), or 'preocupante' (worrying). It is highly versatile and used in both formal writing and everyday conversations.

examples.en_text: My brother's career has taken a very interesting turn since he changed jobs.
examples.target_text: La carrera de mi hermano ha tomado un giro muy interesante desde que cambió de trabajo.

examples.en_text: The weather has taken an unexpected turn and now it is pouring rain.
examples.target_text: El clima ha tomado un giro inesperado y ahora está lloviendo a cántaros.

examples.en_text: Today's meeting has taken a complicated turn when the budget was discussed.
examples.target_text: La reunión de hoy ha tomado un giro complicado cuando se habló del presupuesto.

examples.en_text: The police investigation has taken a decisive turn thanks to a new witness.
examples.target_text: La investigación policial ha tomado un giro decisivo gracias a un nuevo testigo.

examples.en_text: His health has taken a positive turn after starting the new treatment.
examples.target_text: Su salud ha tomado un giro positivo después de empezar el nuevo tratamiento.

examples.en_text: Our science project has taken a surprising turn at the last minute.
examples.target_text: Nuestro proyecto de ciencias ha tomado un giro sorprendente a última hora.
